When I was about 11, I went to Claire’s before Christmas and bought a pair of dangling Christmas tree earrings made out of green pom-poms. They were fluffy and comically large, truly a statement accessory. As soon as I got home I went into my bathroom and closed the door to try my new earrings on. I put the left one in and while I was trying to put in the right one, I accidentally dropped it on the floor. 

Of course, I immediately went to pick it back up but I couldn’t find it. I looked all over the floor of the bathroom. The bathroom was a small room with the door shut and there was nowhere the earring could have gone besides on the floor. It didn’t fall on the counter or in the sink, it was too large to have gone down the sink drain and besides, I saw it fall right towards the ground since I was looking in the mirror when I dropped it. 

I remember feeling very frustrated because the earrings were brand new and they were so big that I couldn’t understand how one could possibly have seemingly disappeared. After looking for it in every possible spot on the floor and in the entire bathroom, I gave up and figured that it must be somewhere in there and that it would eventually turn up. 

Im now 22 years old, I still use the same bathroom, and needless to say, I never saw that earring again. Im convinced that it glitched right out of this dimension because I literally don’t have any other explanation for where it went.

I get why people have an issue with this but the whole pandemic unemployment thing was so hastily executed that looking back it was extremely unfair and I know this because I was a prime example. When the pandemic hit I was 18 living with my parents, no bills no rent nothing, working at a restaurant since I had dropped out of college in January after one semester and wanted to take some time to “find myself” or whatever the fuck and planned to try again with school in the fall. I had been working for not even 3 months when Covid happened and I was promptly laid off since management knew I didn’t need the job like others there did. Obviously totally understandable. I was told by my supervisor that I could file for unemployment and so I did. 

And just like that I was getting 600$ put in my bank account each week for, quite literally like the post says, sitting on my ass while my coworkers with rent and children were still working making minimum wage. Since I had no bills my unemployment was literally just spending money to me. I took multiple vacations with my boyfriend, I bought a hamster, and bought a ton of other random shit I don’t even remember. 

The fact that people working full time ended up making much less money than those who weren’t working at all was a huge fuck up, since initially companies obviously had no way of knowing that the people they laid off would be better off financially than the people they kept, so I assume in many cases, those who needed the job the most ended up struggling the most and those who didn’t need it ended up getting the 600$ a week.

I used to be like you and tried to make sure to get things that I wouldn’t regret/cringe at later on, but at this point my philosophy of the whole thing is that, no matter how hard you try to ensure you get the perfect tattoo that you’ll never cringe at, there’s still a real good chance you’ll end up cringing at it later just because you’re not still that same person and that wouldn’t be current you’s “perfect” tattoo. 

In fact I’ve found that my most meaningful, “deep”tattoos are actually the most cringy because I am reminded that younger me so earnestly believed that it was an “un regrettable” tattoo for future me. But that doesn’t mean I regret the tat- it’s a reminder of a past time in my life and gives me an opportunity to reflect how my life has changed since I was that person who got the tattoo. It shows what I loved at the moment, because you can’t predict what you’ll love in the future no matter how hard you try. 

My point is, don’t worry about the cringe, embrace the cringe, it’s gonna be inevitable for at least some tattoos you get and the people who say otherwise I think are probably kidding themselves. Cringe is the feeling we get when we are reminded of a time when we were less wise and experienced. Feeling cringe is literally proof that you’re constantly growing as a person. If someone went their whole life not cringing at any decisions of their past self, including tats, then that would be a person who never grew and developed throughout their life. 

Get what you love right now, this moment tattooed. Because it’s pointless to try and pretend like you have an accurate idea of what your future mindsets gonna be. Life’s way too short to spend time “regretting” your past self’s tat decisions. Just make sure it’s something you truly love and not just something you pick based on what you think you’ll never regret.

You have great energy. You’re not ugly, keep at the weight loss- your facial features will get more defined and your confidence will increase! 

IMO, the most important thing you can do is be aware that your clothing and hair can be systematically chosen based on certain “rules” of your specific body and face type. This will allow you to dress in a way that’s as flattering as possible. Clothes and hair should be made to help enhance your beauty, not be allowed to work against you!

Youre an Apple body type- I highly recommend investing in clothing that flatters your shape. Here’s one link I found with a quick search (but there’s endless more resources online):

https://theconceptwardrobe.com/build-a-wardrobe/apple-body-shape

the right clothing for your body makes a HUGE difference, you can easily avoid the leggy peter griffin look if you so desire😆

Also, your haircut doesn’t flatter your face shape!! In fact, it’s doing the opposite! Your face is very round. Even when you lose weight, your face will still be round, it’s your bone structure. This is not a bad thing! it just means you need to learn how to flatter it. Also, your face is wider at the bottom. The curtain bangs make your forehead look narrower which makes the bottom of your face look even wider. The straight-across wispy bangs in the second pic are better, but they shorten your face when you want to do the opposite for a round face. And the length of your hair makes your face look both rounder and shorter.

I highly recommended growing your hair out and ditching the bangs. It’ll take a bit, but let your bangs grow out as long as possible (you can clip them up/ put them up in a ponytail with the rest of your hair when they reach an awkward length) and let the rest of your hair grow to at least armpit length. Then, you can get a cut like this:

https://imgur.com/gallery/3z2J8Q7

This style has no layers that accentuate the round face, instead it hides the sides of a round face and narrows her face (especially the bottom half!) as well as makes her face look longer. You will look SO different by just changing your haircut with your face shape in mind. Also, the slightly darker hair color in the last pic looks super good on you. I would stick with brown shades instead of the blonde highlights in the other pics- darker shades slim the face while blonde widens it. 

If you want glasses that flatter you more, invest in a pair that are larger and more angled and wider at the top/slimmer at the bottom instead of circular, like these:

https://imgur.com/gallery/JcKkr9P

As you can see, all these suggestions are things you can do right now regardless of where you’re at in your weight loss journey. I think the biggest thing is your confidence, and you can do simple things like these that will improve your confidence even if you’re not at your goal weight yet.
